feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. The candidate is iteration 3 with two small changes: kd 0.8 to 1.0, and all sensors moved from y = 0.05 to y = 0.06 m. Iteration 3 (score 396.3) remains the best raced design. It finishes the oval 20/20 with zero line-loss events, but fails on the s-bend (progress 0.46, max_error 0.064) and the slalom (progress 0.09). Iteration 4 raised kd to 1.0 together with kp 5.5 and base_speed 1.05, and the oval fell to 13/20, so the oval damage in that run came from the kp and speed changes, not from kd. kd 1.0 alone is therefore untested, and the sensor move is untested too. The sensor move is small (1 cm forward) and keeps the x layout that iteration 3 used. Iteration 6 showed that changing the sensor x span cut the oval to 13/20, so the x layout must stay as it is. Body width is already at its maximum and the 0.06 m limit cannot move, so bend survival has to come from control and sensing. Approve it, because the change is a minimal step from the best design and the race is the only way to learn whether kd or the earlier sensor position helps.

After the race, read the results in this order. (a) If the oval still completes 20/20 with line_loss_events at 0 and s-bend progress rises above 0.5, keep kd 1.0 and y 0.06, then try kd 1.2 next. (b) If the oval completion drops below 1.0 or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3, revert y to 0.05 and keep kd 1.0, because the forward sensor move is the likely cause. (c) If the oval holds but s-bend progress does not move, neither change is the limit; return to y 0.05 and kd 0.8, and test wheel_track 0.09 alone before changing gains again.
requested_changes: If the oval holds at 20/20 and s-bend progress rises above 0.5: keep kd 1.0 and y 0.06, then try kd 1.2 with other fields fixed, because kd is the damping lever that did not hurt the oval when tested alone.

If the oval completion drops below 1.0 or steering_oscillation exceeds 0.3: revert all sensor y to 0.05 and keep kd 1.0, because iteration 6 showed that changing the sensor layout can reduce oval finish, and iteration 4 showed that kp 5.5 and speed 1.05 are the costly changes.

If s-bend progress is flat with the oval holding: return to y 0.05 and kd 0.8 and test wheel_track 0.09 alone, because iterations 1 to 3 showed that a narrower track raised bend progress without losing the oval, while iteration 5 showed that mass 0.5 with wheel_track 0.09 cut the oval to 25%.
